text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Wednesday.

GERMANY - Bund futures drifted at lower levels after slightly stronger than expected third quarter German gdp and weak U.S. Treasuries sparked rounds of selling. Traders said they expected the market to drift sideways between 102.30 and 102.55 ahead of Thursday's Bundesbank council meeting and unemployment numbers.
The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 102.28, down 0.37 from Tuesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts settled lower, spooked by a slightly disappointing auction of five year paper and by Tuesday's sharp fall in sterling. But with the gilt/Bund spread ballooning to 190 basis points from 186 on Tuesday, dealers said some international investors may re-emerge. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 110-18/32 down 23/32 from Tuesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures slipped slightly in late session, with the United States overnight and weaker Bunds following slightly stronger than expected German gross domestic product data. The December bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 129.56 down 0.26 from Tuesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bond futures held to easier levels in late trading reflecting the lower tone to many overseas bond markets and also the lira which retreated from recent highs. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 128.57 down 0.14 from Tuesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries were a bit lower on Wednesday as the dollar steadied. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 115-25/32, down 7/32 from Tuesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.37 percent.

JAPAN - Cash Japanese government bonds (JGBs) were firmer while futures were flat in uneventful Tokyo trading on Wednesday in a market led by technical transactions by dealers. The basis between the cash and futures bonds widened due to the futures market's reluctance to follow the cash JGB gains. In after hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 126.19, down 0.19 from Tuesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary market saw a variety of currencies tapped on Wednesday, but only in small amounts or increases of previously launched issues. The market awaits the launch of Israel's debut Eurobond -- a $200 million five-year offering -- which will be priced to yield around 50 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes, but possibly tighter if investor demand allows, Israeli ministry of finance director-general David Brodet told a press conference.
